51953-the-manager-of-the-b-a-a-novel.title: The Manager Of The B A A Novel
51953-the-manager-of-the-b-a-a-novel.creator: Vaughan Kester
51953-the-manager-of-the-b-a-a-novel.description: A book by Vaughan Kester. Having read the two columns of local and personal gossip arranged under the heading “People You Know,” he swept his newspaper into the wastebasket and pushed back his chair. The window nearest his desk overlooked the yards and a long line of shabby day coaches and battered freight cars on one of the sidings. They were there to be rebuilt or repaired.

arxiv-1902-06050.title: Combination of Domain Knowledge and Deep Learning for Sentiment Analysis of Short and Informal Messages on Social Media
arxiv-1902-06050.description: Abstract Sentiment analysis has been emerging recently as one of the major natural language processing (NLP) tasks in many applications. Especially, as social media channels (e.g. social networks or forums) have become significant sources for brands to observe user opinions about their products, this task is thus increasingly crucial.

arxiv-2207-09306.title: Statistical analysis of proton induced reactions to generate recommended data for the production of medical radio-isotopes
arxiv-2207-09306.creator: Sourav Mondal, A. Gandhi, Rebecca Pachuau
arxiv-2207-09306.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sourav Mondal, A. Gandhi, Rebecca Pachuau. Radio-isotopes produced via proton induced reaction holds special significance regarding nuclear medicine, astrophysical p-process, theragnostic and diagnostic processes. 76 Br, 80m Br and 61 Cu are positron emitter and they are useful in the functional studies via Positron Emission Tomography (PET), whereas 77 Br bears the potential for the application in Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT) which involves electron capture process. PET and SPECT have been in high application in medical physics, diagnostics, therapy and nuclear medicine.

arxiv-2208-09262.title: Byzantine Consensus is Θ ⁡ ( n 2 ) \Theta(n^{2}) The Dolev-Reischuk Bound is Tight even in Partial Synchrony! (Extended Version)
arxiv-2208-09262.creator: Pierre Civit, Muhammad Ayaz Dzulfikar, Seth Gilbert, Vincent Gramoli, Rachid Guerraoui, Jovan Komatovic, Manuel Vidigueira
arxiv-2208-09262.description: Abstract The Dolev-Reischuk bound says that any deterministic Byzantine consensus protocol has (at least) quadratic communication complexity in the worst case. While it has been shown that the bound is tight in synchronous environments, it is still unknown whether a consensus protocol with quadratic communication complexity can be obtained in partial synchrony.

arxiv-2301-03938.title: Consensus based phase connectivity identification for distribution network with limited observability
arxiv-2301-03938.creator: Md Umar Hashmi, David Brummund, Rickard Lundholm, Arpan Koirala, and Dirk Van Hertem
arxiv-2301-03938.description: Abstract The mitigation of distribution network (DN) unbalance and the use of single-phase flexibility for congestion mitigation requires accurate phase connection information, which is often not available. For a large DN, the naïve phase identification proposed in the majority of the prior works using a single voltage reference does not scale well for a multi-feeder DN.

arxiv-2312-04539.title: Auto-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2312-04539.creator: Osman Ülger, Maksymilian Kulicki, Yuki Asano, Martin R. Oswald
arxiv-2312-04539.description: Abstract Open-Vocabulary Segmentation (OVS) methods are capable of performing semantic segmentation without relying on a fixed vocabulary, and in some cases, without training or fine-tuning. However, OVS methods typically require a human in the loop to specify the vocabulary based on the task or dataset at hand.

arxiv-2405-16210.title: Scalar Leptoquark Contribution to Two Photon Elastic Scattering
arxiv-2405-16210.creator: M. Omar Nadeem
arxiv-2405-16210.description: Abstract Abstract We study the contribution of Scalar Leptoquark (SLQ) loops to the two photon scattering cross section at high energies. The leading order helicity amplitudes are discussed at coupling \mathcal{O}(e^{4}) for Standard Model (SM) fermions, weak bosons and SLQs.

arxiv-2406-08070.title: CFG++: Manifold-constrained Classifier Free Guidance for Diffusion Models
arxiv-2406-08070.creator: Hyungjin Chung *, Jeongsol Kim *, Geon Yeong Park *, Hyelin Nam *, Jong Chul Ye
arxiv-2406-08070.description: Abstract Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is a fundamental tool in modern diffusion models for text-guided generation. Although effective, CFG has notable drawbacks. For instance, DDIM with CFG lacks invertibility, complicating image editing; furthermore, high guidance scales, essential for high-quality outputs, frequently result in issues like mode collapse.

arxiv-2408-02221.title: SoK: Fighting Counterfeits with Cyber–Physical Synergy Based on Physically-Unclonable Identifiers of Paper Surface
arxiv-2408-02221.creator: Anirudh Nakra, Min Wu, Chau-Wai Wong
arxiv-2408-02221.description: Abstract Counterfeit products cause severe harm to public safety and health by penetrating untrusted supply chains. Numerous anti-counterfeiting techniques have been proposed, among which the use of inherent, unclonable irregularities of paper surfaces has shown considerable potential as a high-performance economical solution.

arxiv-2410-11172.title: Asynchronous 3-Majority Dynamics with Many Opinions
arxiv-2410-11172.creator: Colin Cooper King’s College London colin.cooper@kcl.ac.uk and Frederik Mallmann-Trenn King’s College London frederik.mallmann-trenn@kcl.ac.uk and Tomasz Radzik King’s College London tomasz.radzik@kcl.ac.uk and Nobutaka Shimizu Institute of Science Tokyo shimizu.n.ah@m.titech.ac.jp and Takeharu Shira
arxiv-2410-11172.description: Abstract We consider 3-Majority, a probabilistic consensus dynamics on a complete graph with n n vertices, each vertex starting with one of k k initial opinions. At each discrete time step, a vertex u u is chosen uniformly at random.

arxiv-2411-06634.title: Inductive Graph Few-shot Class Incremental Learning
arxiv-2411-06634.creator: Yayong Li, Peyman Moghadam, Can Peng, Nan Ye, Piotr Koniusz
arxiv-2411-06634.description: Abstract . Node classification with Graph Neural Networks (GNN) under a fixed set of labels is well known in contrast to Graph Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning (GFSCIL), which involves learning a GNN classifier as graph nodes and classes growing over time sporadically.

arxiv-2504-18388.title: Virial theorem for rigidly rotating matter
arxiv-2504-18388.creator: Sourav Dey
arxiv-2504-18388.description: Abstract The scaling property of the thermodynamic free energy ( Φ \Phi ) of a system at global equilibrium has been examined using a real-time method known as the virial theorem. We demonstrate these scaling properties through a derived relation based on the general structure of equal-time commutators among Poincaré charges and their densities.

pmc-11401207.title: Caecal perforation secondary to intrapelvic migration of a total hip prosthesis: A case report and a review of the literature
pmc-11401207.creator: Imen Ben Ismail, Marwen Sghaier, Saber Rebii, Ghazi Manai, Ayoub Zoghlami
pmc-11401207.description: IntroductionTotal hip arthroplasty (THA) is commonly performed to alleviate hip pain and restore function. While generally safe, complications such as prosthesis migration can occur. Intrapelvic migration of hip prostheses, leading to bowel perforation and fistula formation, is a rare but severe complication requiring prompt diagnosis and management.

pmc-11551054.title: A multi-task prediction method based on neighborhood structure embedding and signed graph representation learning to infer the relationship between circRNA, miRNA, and cancer

pmc-11551054.description: MotivationResearch shows that competing endogenous RNA is widely involved in gene regulation in cells, and identifying the association between circular RNA (circRNA), microRNA (miRNA), and cancer can provide new hope for disease diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. However, affected by reductionism, previous studies regarded the prediction of circRNA-miRNA interaction, circRNA-cancer association, and miRNA-cancer association as separate studies.

pmc-11692379.title: RACIAL/ETHNIC DISPARITIES IN TRAJECTORIES OF CARDIOVASCULAR RISK FACTORS IN US ADULTS
pmc-11692379.creator: Radha Dhingra, Hanzhang Xu, Scott Lynch, Qing Yang, Michael Green, Jessica West, Matthew Dupre
pmc-11692379.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Racial/ethnic disparities in major cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors are well documented. However, studies have not considered racial/ethnic differences in the interrelationships among these CVD risk factors and how they vary across age. We used six waves of longitudinal data from the Health and Retirement Study ([HRS] 2006-2016; n=10,292) to examine co-occurring changes in systolic blood pressure ([BP] mmHg), non-HDL cholesterol (mg/dl), diabetes (y/n), and smoking (y/n) at ages 50-80.

IntroductionWorld-wide, endurance races, including road races, trail races, cycling events, and triathlons, attract millions of participants each year. The World Academy of Endurance Medicine (WAEM) created the Race Emergency Medicine Course (REMC) to train and certify race organizers and medical directors regarding planning and response for medical emergencies at endurance events.
